subject: Standard Errors Could Not be Computed for Data Set(s)

messages.author: b277f4bfe1bf5a8d
messages.subject: Standard Errors Could Not be Computed for Data Set(s)
parts:
Hello everyone,

I am running a CFA of a one-factor model with 5 binary indicators using 20 multiply imputed data sets in lavaan 0.6-9. Here is the syntax I am using:

t6ptsd <-'
t6ptsd=~t6ptsd6r1+t6ptsd4r1+t6ptsd7r1+t6ptsd1r1+t6ptsd5r1
'
t6ptsd.fit <- cfa.mi(t6ptsd,covid.data,estimator="WLSMV", parameterization="theta", ordered=c("t6ptsd6r1","t6ptsd4r1","t6ptsd7r1","t6ptsd1r1","t6ptsd5r1"))
summary(t6ptsd.fit,fit.measures=TRUE,standardized=TRUE,rsquare=TRUE,test="D2",pool.robust=TRUE)

The output tells me that standard errors could not be computed for 18 of the 20 data sets. The suggestion provided in the output is to fit the model to the individual data sets to diagnose the problem. When I fit the model to each individual data set, everything seems to go well. There are no warnings or errors, and standard errors that seem reasonable are provided. I was wondering (1) if anyone might have an idea of why standard errors are computed for the individual data sets using the cfa function but not when the cfa.mi function is used; (2) if there are additional steps that can be taken to diagnose the problem; and (3) if there is a work around that might exist whereby the results of the individual data sets can be pooled in a manner similar to what the cfa.mi function does.

Thanks,

Ryan

messages.author: 6f81c58ba9ed02c3
messages.subject: Re: Standard Errors Could Not be Computed for Data Set(s)
parts:
Hello again everyone,

I figured out the issue, which was definitely user error. In the two data sets that cfa.mi was able to converge on, one of the items was not binary. I'm not entirely sure how that happened, but when I made proper adjustments to those imputed data sets to ensure the item would be binary, cfa.mi was able to converge on all 20 imputed data sets.

Thanks,

Ryan
